newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares end off day's lows.
newsitem.headline: India shares end off day's lows.

text.p: Indian shares ended off their lows on Wednesday, but brokers and analysts said the selling spree would continue for some time on the back of a bearish sentiment.
"More of delivery-based selling is pushing down prices... The retail investors waiting to sell are getting desperate," analyst Nikhil Vora at Ceat Financial Services told Reuters.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's top 30-share index plunged 85 points, or 3.0 percent, in mid-session trading, but recovered slightly to end at 2,754.06, down 52.94.
"It looks as if this fall was expected...we might now see some good values in the market at these levels," said Vora.
Traders said some short-covering in front-bench stocks and buying from local funds stemmed the market's sharp fall on Wednesday, but the outlook remained pessimistic.
"We feel there might be support around the 2,700 level, but it will only be short-lived," said chief dealer S. Ramakrishnan at ASK-Raymond James Securities India Ltd.

Bearish sentiment led to nervous market conditions, with major players also jumping on to the selling bandwagon. "There are many red signals out on the economic front... People are pressing sales in infrastructure stocks," he said.
Ceat Financial's Vora said commodity stocks had taken a sharp hit in the recent fall. "Cement, steel, petrochemicals...are not on the buy list of any firms," he said.
"Correct values for stocks are now being built in... There was too much hype about the cement story."
Gujarat Ambuja Cement, which bore the brunt of selling pressure in recent sessions, ended 4.24 rupees higher at 195.25
Auto stocks Mahindra & Mahindra and TELCO closed slightly higher.
The Bombay index has fallen 145.44 points, or 5.03 percent, this week from last Friday's close of 2,890.50.
India's overseas listed shares fell in London in panicky trade on Wednesday. The James Capel index for Indian GDRs fell 2.71 points, or 4.9 percent, to 52.07 points in early afternoon trade.
